label: Restaurant
recognise: Restaurants, cafés, bakeries, bars, takeaways, food trucks and caterers.
research: What websites of similar restaurants (same cuisine and, if given, the same area) usually show, and what guests look for before they book or order.

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: The food and atmosphere in pictures, signature dishes, opening hours, location and how to book or order.

pages.title: Menu
pages.purpose: The menu by section, with short descriptions, prices and dietary labels where the owner gives them.

pages.title: About us
pages.purpose: The story, the people and what makes the food special.

pages.title: Book a table
pages.purpose: How to reserve, group bookings and private events.

pages.title: Contact
pages.purpose: Address with directions, phone, opening hours and ordering links.

pages.title: Privacy policy
pages.purpose: How booking and contact details are used.

sections.header: The restaurant's name or logo, the menu and main pages, and a Book a table or Order now button.
sections.footer: Address, phone, opening hours, social links, quick links and the privacy policy.
sections.homepage: A big, appetising hero photo with the name and a booking or ordering button; signature dishes; the story in a few lines; opening hours and location from the site details (left out until given); reviews only if the owner gives real ones; a final call to book.

rules: Let photos lead: large images, short text.
Prices, allergens and dietary labels only as the owner gives them.
Opening hours and the address easy to find on every page.
Never invent reviews, ratings or awards.

demo.note: Where the owner gave no menu, write these as sample dishes for them to replace. Samples are only ever offerings like these: never sample people, staff photos, opening hours, prices, addresses or phone numbers.

questions.title: Your menu and signature dishes
questions.lead: Your cuisine, dietary options and a few signature dishes. Prices only if you want them shown.
questions.why: The Menu page and the homepage's signature dishes need them.

fields.label: Signature dishes
fields.hint: Up to 6 for the homepage. Claude writes the full Menu page from these and asks for the rest.

questions.title: Where and when can guests find you?
questions.lead: These go in your site details, the footer and the Contact page.
questions.why: Only you know your address, phone and opening hours.

questions.title: How do guests book a table?
questions.lead: This sets the button in your header and on the homepage.
questions.why: It sets the button in your header.

questions.title: What should it look and feel like?
questions.lead: The atmosphere sets the colours and type; your logo and photos make it yours.
questions.why: Your logo and photos make the site yours.

fields.label: Photos (up to 6)
fields.hint: Your food, your room, your team.

questions.title: Your story and where else to find you
questions.lead: Real words from you make the About page. Reviews only if they're real: we never invent them.
questions.why: Real words for the About page; reviews only if real.

fields.label: Your story in a few sentences
Real guest reviews (optional)
fields.hint: Paste up to 3, each with the guest's name. Leave empty and the site shows none until you add some.

questions.title: Do you deliver or do takeaway?
questions.lead: Delivery-app links sit next to your booking button, so guests can order in one tap.
questions.why: Delivery-app links get orders in one tap.

questions.title: Do you host groups or private events?
questions.lead: Restaurants that take groups say so on the Book a table page.
questions.why: You mention groups: places that seat them say how many.
